title: Service Edge names in logs, APIs and support: ZEN, broker, PSEN, VZEN

prose.text: Current help pages say Service Edge, but older names survive in log fields, API paths and conversation. Where a source shows the older name, it is below.

prose.label: Internet & SaaS logs.
prose.text: ZIA web and firewall logs identify the data center rather than the edge: [[shared.multi-cluster:datacenter-in-logs]].

prose.label: Unconfirmed.
prose.text: The expansions and abbreviations used for each edge (PZEN, PSEN, VSEN and others) are not in a captured source {{gap:legacy-acronyms}}, and neither is the form of edge host names in logs {{gap:edge-hostnames}}.

checks.do: When a log, ticket or runbook says ZEN or broker, read it as a Service Edge and keep the original term when quoting it.
Before reading PZEN as public or private, ask which product and form factor is meant; the abbreviation's expansion is unconfirmed.

connector-zen.statement: In the Private Access user activity log, ConnectorZEN is the Public Service Edge that sent the request from the App Connector.

quotes: ConnectorZEN | The Public Service Edge that sent the request from the App Connector
The Public Service Edge for Private Access that received the request from the Zscaler Client Connector

virtual-zen-api.statement: The ZIA API manages Virtual Service Edge clusters at /virtualZenClusters and Virtual Service Edges at /virtualZenNodes.

expect.description: Retrieves a list of ZIA Virtual Service Edge clusters. .
Retrieves the ZIA Virtual Service Edge for an organization. .

zen-is-service-edge.statement: So ZEN in a Zscaler field or path name denotes a Service Edge: the ZPA log's ClientZEN and ConnectorZEN hold Public Service Edges, and the ZIA API's virtualZen paths hold Virtual Service Edges.
zen-is-service-edge.conditions: Generalizes from the names these sources use; no source defines ZEN.

broker-is-zpa-service-edge.statement: Broker is a name for a Private Access Service Edge: the help describes the ZPA Private Service Edge as a single-tenant broker that provides the functionality of a Public Service Edge for Private Access.
broker-is-zpa-service-edge.conditions: The sources use broker descriptively for the Private Service Edge; no source states that broker is a former product name or names the Public Service Edge a broker.

legacy-acronyms.title: Older names and abbreviations for each Service Edge
legacy-acronyms.detail: Unverified legacy statements: the ZIA Public Service Edge was Public ZEN, Public Zscaler Enforcement Node, PZEN; the Private Service Edge was Private ZEN, also PZEN, with PSEN (Private Service Edge Node) for an instance; the Virtual Service Edge was Virtual ZEN, VZEN, with VSEN for a VM instance; the ZPA Public Service Edge was the ZPA broker, "the canonical on-wire term"; the ZPA Private Service Edge was the private broker or ZPA PSE. No captured source gives these expansions or abbreviations.
legacy-acronyms.blocks: translating an abbreviation in a ticket or runbook with certainty

edge-hostnames.title: Form of Service Edge host names in logs
edge-hostnames.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZEN fields carry values like broker1b.pdx2 or zs2-fra1a; broker host names are instance-level identifiers useful for support correlation, and the suffix (pdx2, fra1a) is the data-center code. No captured source documents the value format.
edge-hostnames.blocks: mapping a log value to a data center
